decisions.conflict: Recycled Polypropylene reduces the carbon footprint and material footprint during manufacturing but might suffer from lower impact resistance, risking premature failure during the use phase.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (h), page 79: use or content of recycled materials
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (t), page 80: lightweight design as expressed through reduction of material consumption
decisions.chief_resolution: Select recycled Polypropylene (rPP) optimized with structural ribbing. This aligns with Annex I (h) on recycled content and Annex I (t) on lightweight design, reducing material footprint while maintaining structural integrity.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the supply chain availability and mechanical specification sheets of high-grade post-consumer recycled polypropylene resins to ensure they meet minimum impact resistance requirements.

options_evaluated: Threaded metal inserts with standard screws
decisions.conflict: Ultrasonic welding minimizes assembly time and material weight but permanently seals the housing, making non-destructive disassembly and repair impossible.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), page 79: avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to reuse, upgrading, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, remanufacturing and recycling
decisions.chief_resolution: Recommend threaded fasteners with standard screw heads (e.g., Torx or Philips) and metal inserts. This directly supports Annex I (b) by enabling non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly for repair and recycling, avoiding permanent welding.
decisions.design_action: Verify the compatibility of standard screw types across all housing joints to minimize the variety of tools required for disassembly.

decisions.conflict: Brushed DC motors are cheap and simple to manufacture with fewer electronic components but have a shorter technical lifetime due to brush wear and lower energy efficiency during use.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components as expressed through technical lifetime
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g), page 79: use or consumption of energy, water and other resources in one or more lifecycle stages
decisions.chief_resolution: Select a high-efficiency Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. This choice optimizes energy efficiency during the use phase under Annex I (g) and dramatically extends the technical lifetime and reliability under Annex I (a) due to the absence of wearing brushes.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of standardized BLDC motor form factors from suppliers to ensure future component interchangeability.

options_evaluated: Active cooling with dedicated auxiliary fan
Passive cooling via optimized ventilation slots and internal heat sinks
Air-path cooling (routing suction airflow over the motor)
decisions.conflict: Air-path cooling uses the vacuum's suction air to cool the motor, saving weight and space, but risks motor contamination and catastrophic failure if the dust filtration system leaks.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components, resistance to stresses or ageing mechanisms
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (q), page 80: emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages of the product, including noise
decisions.chief_resolution: Implement a dual-chamber passive cooling design with optimized ventilation slots separate from the main suction air-path. This protects the motor from fine dust ingress, enhancing durability under Annex I (a), and reduces noise emissions under Annex I (q).
decisions.design_action: Review the thermal limits of the selected motor against the expected heat dissipation of the passive venting geometry.

options_evaluated: Modular cartridge-based architecture (separate motor, battery, and filtration modules)
decisions.conflict: A modular cartridge-based architecture makes replacing individual failed parts incredibly easy for consumers but increases the overall weight, volume, and material footprint due to extra housing walls.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, modularity, compatibility with commonly available tools
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (j), page 79: weight and volume of the product and its packaging
decisions.chief_resolution: Adopt a modular cartridge-based architecture where the battery, motor, and filter are separate, easily swappable modules. The repairability benefits under Annex I (b) outweigh the slight weight increase, preventing premature product disposal.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the physical space requirements and layout of the modular cartridges to ensure they can be accessed without removing unrelated components.

options_evaluated: Cordless with integrated lithium-ion battery pack
Cordless with standardized, user-replaceable battery pack
decisions.conflict: Cordless battery-powered vacuums offer high user convenience but suffer from limited battery lifespans, creating hazardous waste and requiring replacement, whereas corded models have unlimited runtime and lower material footprint.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g), page 79: use or consumption of energy... effect of physical factors on product efficiency
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (r), page 80: amounts of waste generated, including plastic waste... and amounts of hazardous waste generated
decisions.chief_resolution: Choose a cordless design utilizing a standardized, user-replaceable battery pack with a digital battery management system. This minimizes hazardous waste generation under Annex I (r) by allowing the battery to be replaced independently of the vacuum, while maintaining energy efficiency under Annex I (g).
decisions.design_action: Check the mechanical and electrical interface standards of major open-battery alliances to ensure compatibility with widely available consumer battery packs.
